Entra/managed identity and eventual least-privilege bindings remain mandatory without an invented administration answer.
The original ten-field service/security form is answered under its own unchanged saved request; this new ID is not a receipt for that earlier response.
Only notification_delivery_scope is a triggered follow-up: its when.equals is the complete actual normalized notification_channels selection, including both channel capabilities and simulation-only.

Batch C asks once about independent messaging need with None and guidance routes, and only missing supporting-product preferences. Required identity, monitoring, secrets, registry/image delivery and secure remote access/private DNS are prerequisites, not optional waivers.

3i reuses explicitly selected App Service Linux containers, Cosmos primary store, no relational store and Blob storage. Resolve the real notification scope conflict in the follow-up; do not ask redundant whole-scope approval or infer optional additions.

3j covers the already-confirmed App Service, Cosmos and storage-replication classes, commitments and dev-only overrides in this batch. No pin, floor, commitment or no-preference answer exists yet; do not set sku_preferences_captured before actual answers and any newly applicable classes are reconciled.

No registry, Key Vault, monitoring, identity or notification transport SKU is creatively derived here. If the returned supporting/messaging choice adds a creative-SKU class, elicit only that newly applicable class later.

form.message: Project Fulcrum — final known-platform preferences and one clarification. Captured, not asked again: dev only; Balanced; App Service Linux containers; Cosmos DB as preferred primary store; no relational database; private Blob media/documents; workforce plus external Volunteer sign-in; a new secure remote-access path; policy-conditional authenticated public monitoring; existing platform/team monitoring access; 30-day sanitized diagnostics. Sweden Central ONLY is a strict residency constraint for all capabilities, including identity and notifications; feasibility remains for Architecture, with no global-service exemption assumed. You selected email + mobile push AND simulation-only: clarify delivery scope below without losing the channel intent. Other fields are independent missing preferences. No SKU preference lets Architecture choose the least-cost suitable option meeting Balanced and all captured requirements. No real contacts, identifiers or destinations; no purchase, deployment or Gate 1 approval is requested.

notification_delivery_scope.title: Email and push — resolve dev delivery versus simulation
notification_delivery_scope.description: The original three choices are all retained. Which MVP transport scope did you intend? Every route remains subject to Sweden Central-only residency, fictional dev data and safe delivery controls. No feasibility or current outbound permission is inferred. A custom explanation uses this same field.
enum: Actual email + push transports — provision and test with fictional accounts/dev destinations
Email + push integrations in scope — simulate all outbound in MVP
Simulation-only MVP — defer email/push transports, retain functional channel intent
Not sure — guide me; no outbound delivery permission

messaging_events.title: Async platform — separate queue or event-service need
messaging_events.description: Notifications alone do not establish a need for a broker. Recommendation: None unless you already know of a separate asynchronous/integration need. Select only known needs, or None/guidance alone; custom needs use this same field. Nothing is added by default.

enum: None — no separate messaging/event service required
Service Bus — transactional queues/topics are a known requirement
Event Hubs — high-throughput event ingestion is a known requirement
Event Grid — cloud event distribution is a known requirement
Storage Queues — lightweight queues are a known requirement
Not sure — Architect assess; do not add without justification

supporting_services.title: Supporting dependencies — missing product preferences
supporting_services.description: Monitoring, secrets/certificates, container image delivery, workforce/external identity and secure private access/DNS remain prerequisites regardless of this answer. Choose only product preferences you already have, or a recommendation route alone. Unchecked products are not a waiver of prerequisites. Monitoring access stays with the existing platform/team. Architecture owns identity/access design and residency feasibility; no gateway, edge, microservices or optional service is added here. Custom preferences use this field.

enum: Azure Monitor + Application Insights + Log Analytics — preferred diagnostics products
Key Vault — preferred secrets/certificates service
Azure Container Registry — preferred container image registry
No supporting-product preference — Architect recommend required dependencies only
Not sure — guide me; required dependencies remain in scope

sku_app_service.title: App Service Linux container host — SKU or tier-floor preference
sku_app_service.description: Only capture a hard preference you already know, not a technical design. Balanced and private API access still apply. Enter an exact pin or minimum tier in this same field; do not select a generic pin/floor label without the value. No preference does not relax security, recovery, residency or budget objectives.
enum: No SKU preference — Architect choose least-cost suitable tier meeting captured requirements
Pinned SKU/size — enter the exact value in this field
Tier floor only — enter the minimum tier in this field

sku_nosql.title: Cosmos primary store — throughput-mode or capacity preference
sku_nosql.description: The primary store preference is already captured. If you have a hard throughput-mode, capacity or tier-floor preference, enter it here; otherwise leave sizing to Architecture. No capacity, second store or cross-region replication is inferred. A custom answer uses this same field.
enum: No SKU preference — Architect choose least-cost suitable tier meeting captured requirements
Pinned throughput mode/capacity — enter the exact value in this field
Tier or capacity floor only — enter the minimum in this field

sku_storage_repl.title: Private Blob storage — single-region replication preference
sku_storage_repl.description: Sweden Central-only excludes geo/cross-region replication. LRS keeps local copies; ZRS distributes copies across zones within one region, subject to service availability and feasibility checks. No preference leaves the suitable in-region choice to Architecture. Custom preferences use this same field; nothing here permits public blobs or shared-key shortcuts.
enum: No SKU preference — Architect choose least-cost suitable tier meeting captured requirements
LRS — explicit locally redundant replication pin
ZRS — explicit same-region zone-redundant replication pin
Tier floor or custom in-region constraint — enter it in this field

sku_commitment.title: Dev platform pricing — reservation commitment preference
sku_commitment.description: Capture a known commercial preference only, across applicable services. The USD 500–2,000 monthly soft planning range remains unchanged. A reservation preference is not purchasing or spend authorization. A custom answer uses this same field.
enum: On-demand only — no reserved commitment
Reserved 1-year preference — no purchase authorization
Reserved 3-year preference — no purchase authorization
No commitment preference — Architect recommend; no purchase authorization

sku_env_override.title: Dev-only scope — environment-specific SKU overrides
sku_env_override.description: Only dev is in this delivery. Do not define Production or reopen environment scope. Identify any different dev-specific pin/floor in this same field; otherwise apply the preferences above to dev only. Custom overrides must identify the applicable class and actual value.
enum: No dev-specific SKU override — apply these preferences to dev only
Dev-only SKU override — enter the class and exact pin/floor in this field

answers.industry: Nonprofit community support for vulnerable individuals and families; volunteer-led experiences and support
answers.budget_limit: Planning target — optimize and highlight overruns
answers.recovery_profile: Standard — recover within 4 hours; up to 1 hour of data loss
answers.performance_target: Typical API responses under 2 seconds — planning goal to validate
answers.private_client_access: A new secure remote-access path is needed
answers.authentication_requirement: Employees plus external Volunteers — fictional dev accounts
answers.non_relational_store: Cosmos DB — preferred primary document store
notification_channels: Mobile push capability — fictional/dev testing only
Dev simulation only — no outbound delivery
answers.monitoring_network_requirement: Authenticated public monitoring permitted if policy allows
answers.monitoring_access_scope: An existing platform/team handles monitoring access
answers.current_delivery_scope: New dev-only hosting-platform MVP; first usable infrastructure within two weeks. Future Production is outside this delivery.
answers.current_delivery_data_constraint: Development uses fictional data only. Mandatory security/privacy baseline applies in dev; future Production GDPR requirement remains outside this dev delivery, with no compliance certification.
answers.system_description: Infrastructure-only hosting platform and cloud services for a secure, intuitive, mobile-first Volunteer engagement MVP, including support for a containerized backend. All application development is handled by another team and is out of scope.
answers.business_objective: Reduce manual coordination and administrative overhead; improve Volunteer engagement and matching, opportunity discovery, assignments, approvals, tracking, reporting, visibility and communication; accelerate assignments and grow without proportional administration.
answers.delivery_context: New MVP; pro bono initiative for The Organization. Existing coordination relies on calls, email, instant messaging, spreadsheets and manual approvals/follow-ups, causing overhead, low visibility and poor scalability. This is business context, not a migration request.
infrastructure_scope: Hosting support for a containerized backend; backend code excluded
Notification platform capabilities, with channels still to evaluate
Store anonymous resulting documentation in this repository
application_scope_exclusions: Detailed business workflow, escalation and reporting implementation
answers.application_role_constraints: Initial permission boundaries require Project Stakeholders validation. Manager is a functional role, not an identifiable party. Exact permissions and application implementation belong to another team.
answers.configurable_workflow_intent: Volunteer registration, participation approval, assignment confirmation, cancellations and changes. Exact rules and escalation remain undefined, belong to the application team, and do not block platform intake.
answers.operational_reporting_intent: Opportunities, registrations, assignment status, completed activities and participation. Detailed reports and impact metrics require application stakeholder confirmation.
answers.technology_evaluation_constraints: Candidates are not mandatory selections. Evaluate alternatives for suitability, security, simplicity, maintainability, scale and cost within limited nonprofit budgets; challenge complexity and avoid overengineering.
answers.design_preferences_not_decisions: Prefer managed services and a modular monolith; no microservices absent clear justification.
answers.data_processing_constraints: Personal Volunteer information and sensitive organizational activity may be processed. Beneficiary data is not assumed. Never use real personal information in development or testing; fictional sample data only.
security_privacy_requirements: Secure authentication and role-based access control
Encryption in transit and at rest
compliance: GDPR required for Production. MVP must be GDPR-aligned; the supplied brief says MVP does not have to be compliant. This release distinction does not waive applicable legal duties or mandatory security/privacy controls. Do not certify compliance.
anonymity_requirements: Anonymous generated source, documentation, commits, issues, pull requests, test data, infrastructure-as-code and artifacts
No customer/nonprofit or technology-partner names, individual names, real domains, organizational identifiers, correspondence or real beneficiary/Volunteer information
Use only generic party labels: The Organization, Technology Contributors, Volunteers, Coordinators, Administrators, Project Stakeholders
Do not request real names, personal emails, domains or identities during discovery
Do not publish repository remote URLs or account identities in project documentation
Author attribution uses agent role only; no people
answers.recommendation_provenance_requirement: Reasonable recommendations must be labelled Assumption/Recommendation, never represented as user-confirmed values or permission.
answers.sku_pin_evidence: No SKU locks were volunteered. This is not an explicit no-preference response and does not complete SKU elicitation.
answers.authorized_current_activity: Bounded Step 1 requirements discovery, anonymous documentation, validation and the required independent review through the interactive parent. No Azure reads or writes, credential operations, deployment, infrastructure code, application scaffolding, commits or pushes are authorized.
